title: The Sadducees
lead: A Jewish party of the late Second Temple period, linked with the priestly aristocracy and the high priest's families, who accepted the written law of Moses but rejected the Pharisees' traditions and denied the resurrection of the dead. They disappear from history after the temple's destruction in AD 70.

sections.b: The name probably comes from Zadok, the priest of Solomon's day (1 Kings 2:35). Josephus says the Sadducees accepted only the written laws, denied that the soul survives death or that there are rewards and punishments after it, and had the support of the wealthy rather than the people (Antiquities 13.297–298; 18.16–17; Jewish War 2.164–166). In the Gospels they question Jesus about the resurrection (Matthew 22:23–33). In Acts they oppose the apostles' preaching of the resurrection (Acts 4:1–2; 5:17) and are divided from the Pharisees when Paul names the resurrection hope (Acts 23:6–8). Acts 23:8 adds that they deny "angel" and "spirit," a claim whose meaning is debated.
